Saite.et: From Middle High German seite, from Old High German seita (also seito m), from Proto-West Germanic *saidā, *saidō, from Proto-Germanic *saidô (“string, cord”). In the 17th century, the ⟨ei⟩ was changed to the homophonous ⟨ai⟩, in order to distinguish this word…

saisonal.et: From Saison + -al. A pseudo-Gallicism, perhaps modeled on English seasonal (compare French saisonnier).

Saibling.et: Originally Bavarian variant of Sälmling, equivalent to Salm (“salmon”) + -ling. The form shows -a- from secondary umlaut, vowelisation of -l-, and dissimilation -ml- > -bl-. Especially the former two are typically Bavarian developments.

Saitenspiel.et: From Middle High German seitspil, seitespil, seitenspil. By surface analysis, Saite (“string”) + -n- + Spiel (“play”).
